thread.title: Apple, Qualcomm battle over possible ban on some U.S. iPhone imports

author: Channel365
title: Apple, Qualcomm battle over possible ban on some U.S. iPhone imports
text:
(Reuters) – The staff of the U.S. International Trade Commission on Friday advised that a trade judge discover that Apple Inc ( AAPL.O) infringed at least among Qualcomm Inc’s ( QCOM.O) patents, a relocation that might result in blocking the import of some iPhones.
SUBMIT PHOTO: A female looks at the screen of her smart phone in front of an Apple logo outside its store in Shanghai, China July 30, 2017. REUTERS/Aly Song/File Picture
The San Diego chipmaker filed a problem versus Apple nearly a year earlier, asking the commission to prohibit the import of iPhones consisting of competing chipmaker Intel Corp’s ( INTC.O) so-called modem chips, which help mobile phones link to wireless information networks.
At a trial in Washington that began on Friday, the ITC personnel said Apple broke one of Qualcomm’s patents around battery-saving technology.
FILE PHOTO: An indication on the Qualcomm school is seen in San Diego, California, U.S. November 6, 2017. REUTERS/Mike Blake/File Photo
The ITC personnel functions as a 3rd celebration in such trade cases. The staff attorneys’ viewpoints are not binding, however judges frequently follow them.
In previous filings in the ITC case, Apple has argued that Qualcomm’s patents are invalid and that, regardless, the judge should not prohibit Intel-based iPhones due to the fact that it would give Qualcomm a monopoly on modems in the United States and drive Intel from the modem company.
“Qualcomm is selectively asserting its patents to target just Apple products including Intel chipsets– although its patent violation claims would use similarly to Apple items including Qualcomm chipsets– in an attempt to use the ITC as another system for perpetuating its ill-gotten monopoly position,” Apple wrote.
The ITC case is the first to go to trial out of more than a dozen legal fights between Apple and Qualcomm over patents, licensing practices and contracts between the 2. A decision is expected by January.
If the ITC judge chooses to prohibit some iPhone imports, Qualcomm might utilize that to aim to encourage Apple to settle or drop several of the other patent and contract cases, legal professionals have stated.
Apple has argued that a few of Qualcomm’s practices are prohibited, and the chipmaker has paid billions of dollars in fines from antitrust regulators in numerous countries, though it is still appealing some of those judgments.
Qualcomm says its practices are legal and were accepted by clients for several years as the smart device industry flourished, however it has actually made some changes to its licensing model of taking a cut of the asking price of a gadget in a bid to alleviate stress with customers and regulators.
Reporting by Jan Wolfe in Washington, and Stephen Nellis in San Francisco; Editing by Cynthia Osterman
